---
title: "Class Imbalance: Can Prediction Be Improved?"
subtitle: "STAT 447/847 Course Project, Team 2"
author:
  - "John Anyanso"
  - "Nidhi Prajapati"
  - "Ambali Wadud (STAT 847)"
date: "November 29, 2026"
abstract: |
  When one class is rare, a classifier can be very accurate and still useless.
  Three remedies are commonly used: resampling the training data, weighting
  the rare class, and moving the classification threshold. We asked whether
  these remedies improve *prediction* (how well the model ranks positives
  above negatives) or only improve a *metric* (sensitivity at a fixed
  cutoff). We simulated 1,600 data sets from a known logistic model across
  four prevalences, two sample sizes and two levels of class separation,
  fitted lasso logistic regression and random forests with each remedy, and
  then repeated the comparison on 284,807 real credit card transactions.
  Every remedy raised sensitivity, often from below 0.1 to about 0.7, but for
  logistic regression none improved ROC-AUC or PR-AUC, and resampling and
  weights distorted the predicted probabilities. Moving the threshold gave
  the same sensitivity with no refitting and honest probabilities. Random
  forests behaved differently: under-sampling, and on the real data SMOTE,
  improved their ranking when positives were very rare. As the STAT 847
  extension we built EasyEnsemble, which helped forests but not logistic
  regression. An independent second implementation of the study reached the
  same conclusions.
